newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-FERGUSON DELIGHTED AS UNITED FINISH PORTO JOB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON DELIGHTED AS UNITED FINISH PORTO JOB.

text.p: Manchester United became the first English team to reach the semifinals of the European Cup for 12 years on Wednesday but their triumph was marred by crowd trouble.
Their 0-0 draw in the second leg of their quarter-final against Porto gave them a 4-0 aggregate victory following their comprehensive win at Old Trafford two weeks ago.

It was the first time that an English side had reached the last four of Europe's top club competition since Liverpool beat Panathinaikos of Greece 5-0 on aggregate in 1985 before losing to Juventus in the ill-fated final at Belgium's Heysel stadium when 39 fans were killed.
Porto, European champions 10 years ago, began the game as if believing that the 4-0 deficit could be overcome.

They had a series of chances in the opening minutes when United needed all the experience of their Danish international goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel to prevent the Portuguese getting the early break they desperately needed.
Lanky Brazilian striker Mario Jardel went close with two efforts while midfielder Rui Jorge blasted the ball over the crossbar with the goal at his mercy.
"We survived those first 20 minutes due to the good form of Schmeichel," said delighted United coach Alex Ferguson, when the extent of the crowd trouble was still not known.
He said that he felt his side had probably been too cautious and that their counter-attacks had lacked bite. "But I am very, very pleased with the result," he said.
Ferguson declined to be drawn on his team's chances against Borussia Dortmund who beat France's Auxerre 4-1 on aggregate to book their ticket to the semis.
"Borussia have good players with a lot of experience. The main thing is for us to play to our true form," he said.
United had few clear chances against the bustling Portuguese. The closest to goal was probably in the first half when David Beckham sent a 40-yard free-kick crashing against the crossbar.
But the night was marred for United as several English fans were taken to hospital with wounds caused by rubber bullets fired by Portuguese police in incidents as the match was drawing to a close.
Dozens of United fans ignored a police call to remain in the ground after the end of the game, to let the local supporters leave first, and sought to force one of the exit doors.
Ambulance officals said that at least seven United fans were taken to hospital with wounds from plastic bullets and one of them had a bullet lodged in his head.
A number of other fans and police were also injured in the clash which was the second involving United supporters on Wednesday night.
Earlier, around 20 had been slightly hurt when a group of supporters without the right tickets sought to force their way into the ground. They were eventually let in.
It was not immediately known whether there were any arrests.
